A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with SAC-GPT-2, DQN-GPT-2, and DTQN on MiniGrid-Memory and Passive T-Maze in Sections 6.1–6.2 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds POPGym evaluations and an offline DT versus BC-LSTM sequence-length study in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Figures 4 and 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same event-recall identification, context-memory boundary calculation, and STM/LTM testing steps. The additional agents are evaluated comparison methods; no new proposed architecture, loss, or memory mechanism replaces the original framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on POPGym-Autoencode and POPGym-RepeatPrevious, extending coverage beyond the two maze tasks. It also adds testing on unseen, longer T-Maze sequences. The other environments listed in the new horizon-estimation table are not demonstrated as additional training or evaluation benchmarks.

E2.justification: The three online agents from v1 are retained. v2 introduces Decision Transformer and BC-LSTM as evaluated comparators in the new offline T-Maze experiment, substantially extending the comparison to a recurrent memory mechanism.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an offline evaluation protocol spanning seven training sequence lengths from 9 to 900 and eleven validation lengths up to 9600. Appendix F.1 specifies 200 training epochs for DT and 100 for BC-LSTM. Figure 4 also introduces context/horizon configurations for the new POPGym experiments; the original maze settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a substantial generalization analysis comparing performance within and beyond training lengths, including failures after training on long sequences. Figure 4 extends context-versus-horizon sensitivity tests to two POPGym tasks. The original fixed-versus-variable MiniGrid analysis remains.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix E.2 and v2 Appendix F.1 specify the same three runs with different initializations, validation seeds 0–99, and mean results with standard errors. The new heatmaps follow this existing mean-and-SEM reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original maze findings are retained, while v2 adds POPGym results and the Figure 6 heatmaps. BC-LSTM trained at sequence lengths 9–150 achieves 1.00 success through validation length 9600, whereas DT falls to approximately 0.5 beyond its training length. BC-LSTM trained at 600 or 900 performs near chance. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over matching v1 results.

T1.justification: v2 adds a proof of Corollary 1 relating the Markovian case to correlation horizons of one; v1 states the corresponding corollary without proof. The context-memory boundary theorem and its proof are retained. The Meta-RL definition moves from v1's appendix into the main text without a substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain the original taxonomy and evaluation-framework claims. v2's conclusion adds a specific empirical claim distinguishing the short-term memory of the tested transformers from BC-LSTM's long-term memory, modestly extending the central conclusions.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies BC-LSTM's long-term memory capability by the training regimes in which it learns successfully and invokes vanishing gradients to explain failures. It also explains how restricted evaluation can misleadingly favor DT. Appendix C adds explicit STM/LTM classifications for several architecture families; the original interpretation of memory-test configuration remains.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds extensive DT and BC-LSTM architecture, optimizer, context, and training-budget specifications in Tables 7–9; the original online hyperparameters are retained. A new reproducibility statement reports code, scripts, and configurations submitted as an anonymous supplement, although the PDF provides no usable repository locator. Offline dataset construction remains unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references for offline agents, newer memory mechanisms, and benchmarks, including Chen et al., Le et al., and Morad et al. It explicitly distinguishes its RL taxonomy from Yue et al.'s memory-dependency-pair approach. The central positioning around inconsistent memory definitions remains unchanged, despite extensive rewriting of Section 3.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Human-memory background moves earlier, the POMDP section moves to Appendix D, and the Meta-RL definition moves into the main text. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v1's three-panel T-Maze Figure 5 becomes part of v2's nine-panel Figure 4. v2 adds two generalization heatmaps, a horizon-estimation table, and offline hyperparameter tables. Conceptual figures are relocated, the taxonomy table is reformatted, and v1's appendix environment illustration is removed.

improvement.justification: The added POPGym tests and recurrent comparator strengthen evidence beyond v1's maze experiments with attention-based agents. Figure 6 usefully distinguishes length generalization from training failure, and the horizon table and offline settings improve practical usefulness. However, POPGym configurations and offline data construction remain insufficiently documented. Section 5.3's broad statement that DT fails for L > 90 also conflicts with Figure 6's successful longer in-context cases. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall gain.
